title: TMDB daily ID exports
finding: Daily compressed files contain line-delimited ID records, not complete details. Exports cover movies, series, people, collections, networks, keywords and production companies. Files are normally available by 08:00 UTC and retained for three months.
implementation_decision: Use exports for inventory; fetch details separately. A current inventory cannot reconstruct the January catalog.

title: TMDB change tracking
finding: Movie, person and TV changed-ID lists default to the preceding day and can cover up to fourteen days. Individual changes provide field-level information.
implementation_decision: Checkpoint updates; a longer outage requires reconciliation. Do not claim an unlimited historical archive.

title: TMDB API FAQ
finding: Noncommercial API use requires attribution. Commercial use requires contacting TMDB. Approved logo and a non-endorsement notice belong in an About or Credits section. No service-level guarantee is provided.
implementation_decision: Provide Settings → Credits, approved logo and required notice; API access does not grant every underlying media right.

title: TMDB rate limiting
finding: The former ten-second limit was removed. Current protective limits are roughly forty requests per second and may change; clients must honor HTTP 429.
implementation_decision: Default to a conservative bounded request rate; retry/backoff is mandatory, not permission to scrape aggressively.

title: TMDB movie watch providers
finding: The endpoint supplies country-specific provider availability using JustWatch data, requires JustWatch attribution, and does not supply full content deep links.
implementation_decision: Keep availability distinct from ownership, commissioning and historical window evidence; retain provided TMDB link.

title: TMDB image URL construction
finding: Image URLs combine configured base URL, supported size and record path. Company/network SVG logos use original size; PNG alternatives are supported.
implementation_decision: Cache configuration, deduplicate paths and use measured pack sizes. Do not assume all people have portraits.

title: Movie details
finding: Movie detail supports append_to_response with up to twenty appended endpoints.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /movie/{movie_id}. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Series details
finding: Series detail supports append_to_response.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /tv/{series_id}. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Aggregate series credits
finding: Aggregate credits cover cast and crew across episodes, rather than only the newest season.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /tv/{series_id}/aggregate_credits. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Person combined credits
finding: Combined credits cover a person’s movie and television work.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /person/{person_id}/combined_credits. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Movie release dates
finding: Release types are premiere=1, limited theatrical=2, theatrical=3, digital=4, physical=5, TV=6.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /movie/{movie_id}/release_dates. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Season details
finding: Season detail is separately addressable by series and season number.
implementation_decision: Documented API path: /tv/{series_id}/season/{season_number}. Store stable IDs and versioned retrieval dates; no authenticated catalog call was made here.

title: Nielsen public Top Ten
finding: The retrieved streaming chart reports U.S. television viewing for persons aged two and older, ranked by minutes. Its visible period was October 26–November 1, 2026.
implementation_decision: Preserve geography, device scope and units. Never equate minutes with unique people or Netflix views.

title: Netflix Top Ten methodology update
finding: The June 2023 update ranks by views computed from hours divided by runtime and extends most-popular measurement to 91 days. Weekly periods run Monday–Sunday and results publish Tuesday; seasons are measured separately. Older text on the same page describes superseded metrics.
implementation_decision: Version methodology by effective date. Do not apply the older hours ranking or 28-day window to current records.

title: Netflix current weekly chart
finding: The retrieved English-language global film chart covers November 2–8, 2026 and displays rounded millions of views.
implementation_decision: Included values preserve display precision. Publication availability is inferred from MET02 and marked accordingly, not claimed observed.

title: Netflix most-popular film chart
finding: The retrieved chart describes first-91-day views rather than unlimited lifetime viewing.
implementation_decision: Do not label this a lifetime total or mix it with annual television audience rankings.

title: The Numbers data access
finding: OpusData is a subscription-based structured data service covering dated box-office measures. The public site permits personal reference but reserves systematic copying, scraping and redistribution for licensed customers.
implementation_decision: No bulk box-office scrape is included. Accept a licensed import or separately authorized data. Full 2026 box-office replay remains a data-access gap.

title: Netflix pitch policy
finding: Netflix does not accept unsolicited material directly. Pitches require an appropriate representative with an existing relationship; acquisition can also occur through festivals and other established venues.
implementation_decision: Expose represented pitch and acquisition routes, not guaranteed direct upload; keep acceptance uncertain.

title: Prime Video Direct landing
finding: Prime Video Direct describes rent/buy distribution with no setup or recurring submission-management charge.
implementation_decision: Submission fee zero does not imply zero delivery costs or guaranteed publication.

title: Prime licensing and review
finding: Prime distinguishes rent/buy consideration from solicited subscription licensing. Publication is discretionary; eligibility does not guarantee acceptance or a date. Performance reviews can remove titles.
implementation_decision: Separate TVOD submission, SVOD invitation, review and removal states. No automatic subscription listing on upload.

title: Apple approved delivery partners
finding: Aggregators can deliver and manage transactional titles and receive Apple payments before paying owners. Direct delivery requires an agreement; approved encoding houses handle delivery.
implementation_decision: Model Apple transactional delivery separately from Apple subscription commissioning. Track aggregator receivable and settlement.

title: Apple territory language requirements
finding: Transactional delivery requirements depend on storefront language assets for the full film and preview. Noncompliance is surfaced in title and rights/pricing details.
implementation_decision: A territory release requires applicable language delivery; subtitle choices have costs and eligibility effects.

title: Vimeo On Demand seller instructions
finding: The retrieved page announces closure on November 20, 2026, and says new subscriptions/renewals are disabled after September 21, 2026. It points new sellers toward Vimeo OTT.
implementation_decision: Treat this as a dated winding-down service, not an evergreen route. Announcement date is not established here; do not expose the notice in January by guessing.

title: Vimeo On Demand charges
finding: The seller share is ninety percent after transaction costs, not ninety percent of every gross purchase without deductions.
implementation_decision: Use separate cost and share bases. This is a reference fact, not authorization to add a full tax engine.

title: YouTube Partner Program
finding: The retrieved page lists 1,000 subscribers plus either 4,000 qualifying annual watch hours or ten million qualifying Shorts views in ninety days, with review and policy requirements. It also announces a 2027 terms change.
implementation_decision: Uploading alone does not earn ad revenue. Preserve current and announced-future policy versions; no guaranteed RPM or revenue.

title: WB Shyamalan announcement
finding: On February 16, 2023, Warner announced a multi-year directing/producing first-look arrangement involving M. Night Shyamalan and Blinding Edge Pictures, for Warner Bros. Pictures and New Line projects.
implementation_decision: Use as a historical film-deal precedent, not proof it remains active in 2026 or a source of exact financial terms. Discard the page’s implausible box-office typo.

title: WBTV Paul Feig announcement
finding: On April 22, 2025, WBTV announced a multi-year first-look television agreement with Paul Feig and Laura Fischer through Feigco, covering multiple production forms and platforms. Financial terms were undisclosed.
implementation_decision: TV scope may span scripted, unscripted and animation. Retain unknown term expiry and money; simulated offers must say their numbers are modeled.

title: Sony Appian Way announcement
finding: Sony announced a multi-picture, multi-year scripted-feature first-look agreement with Appian Way on August 13, 2020.
implementation_decision: Historical precedent only; do not set a current agreement, expiry or fee from this announcement.

title: Sony–Netflix window agreement
finding: The 2021 announcement describes a U.S. pay-one window after theatrical/home-entertainment releases beginning with the 2022 slate, plus a direct-streaming first look.
implementation_decision: Distinct territory, window and agreement scope are necessary; this announcement does not establish all current global rights.

title: 98th Oscars results
finding: The ceremony took place March 15, 2026 and honored 2025 releases. Included reference records transcribe the four acting categories only.
implementation_decision: Nomination and win are separate events. Four complete acting categories are not the full Oscars roster.

title: 98th nominations announcement
finding: Nominations were announced January 22, 2026; the ceremony was scheduled for March 15.
implementation_decision: Gate nominee visibility from January 22 and winner visibility from ceremony date; exact result timestamps are not supplied.

title: 98th general and Best Picture eligibility
finding: General-entry features exceed forty minutes and require a qualifying seven-day theatrical run in a listed U.S. metro during 2025. Best Picture has additional representation/inclusion and expanded-release requirements.
implementation_decision: Do not equate general-entry eligibility with Best Picture eligibility or apply 2025 windows to 2026 productions.

title: 98th complete rules
finding: Animated-feature rules specify more than forty minutes and animation of primary subjects for at least seventy-five percent of runtime excluding credits. Multiple qualification routes exist.
implementation_decision: Animation is not a binary tag sufficient to qualify. The included rule extract is partial; missing rule branches remain unknown.

title: 78th Emmy calendar
finding: Eligibility runs June 1, 2025–May 31, 2026. Entries close May 7; general nominations July 8; some panel nominations July 15; Creative Arts September 5–6; telecast September 14.
implementation_decision: Use distinct edition/calendar events. Version one is the retrieved document, not proof of no later amendments.

title: International Emmy 2026 checklist
finding: The checklist identifies first broadcast/screening/streaming during January–December 2025, primarily non-U.S. production and initial non-U.S. or simultaneous release; entry deadline January 31, 2026.
implementation_decision: This resolves the earlier missing eligibility-period issue. Checklist is not a complete category rulebook.

title: 78th Emmy comedy series results
finding: The retrieved category page identifies Widow’s Bay, Apple TV, as winner.
implementation_decision: Program result only in this package; do not assign all listed producers awards without importing the full recipient record.

title: 78th Emmy drama series results
finding: The retrieved category page identifies The Pitt, HBO Max, as winner.
implementation_decision: Preserve category and service label as recorded; do not infer ownership from the service.

title: 78th Emmy limited/anthology results
finding: The retrieved category page identifies DTF St. Louis, HBO Max, as winner.
implementation_decision: Keep limited/anthology category distinct from drama series. Included data is not all Emmys competitions.

title: BAFTA 2026 announcement
finding: BAFTA announced film winners on February 22, 2026. One Battle After Another won Best Film; performance winners include Jessie Buckley, Robert Aramayo, Sean Penn and Wunmi Mosaku.
implementation_decision: Separate Best Film and acting recognition; only included verified records count as imported.

title: BAFTA 2026 category results
finding: The score nominees identify Ludwig Göransson/Sinners, Jerskin Fendrix/Bugonia, Alexandre Desplat/Frankenstein, Max Richter/Hamnet and Jonny Greenwood/One Battle After Another.
implementation_decision: These support real composer identities and work credits, not fees, availability or skill ratings.

title: Cannes 2026 results
finding: The May 23 results include Fjord for the Palme d’Or and Minotaure for the Grand Prix. Best Director is shared between La Bola Negra’s directors and Fatherland’s director.
implementation_decision: Allow multiple recipients and tied winning works; not one winner per category in all cases.

title: Cannes feature rules 2026
finding: Selection criteria include production in the preceding twelve months, restrictions on international festival/foreign/Internet exhibition, and a French theatrical-release commitment for Competition features.
implementation_decision: Check premiere history and section-specific obligations before submission. Eligible does not mean selected.

title: Cannes short rules 2026
finding: Competition shorts cannot exceed fifteen minutes including credits and have prior-exhibition restrictions.
implementation_decision: Do not apply the feature or Oscars runtime definition to Cannes shorts; boundaries differ by edition/section.

title: Venice 83 official results
finding: The September 12, 2026 announcement awards the Golden Lion to Woman Unknown and Grand Jury Prize to Possible Love.
implementation_decision: Included result records are selected examples, not full sections or all festival nominations.

title: Sundance 2026 awards announcement
finding: January 30 results identify Josephine, Nuisance Bear, Shame and Money and To Hold a Mountain as the four competition grand-jury winners.
implementation_decision: Separate four competition identities and retain announcement date.

title: SXSW 2026 jury awards
finding: March 18 announcement identifies Wishful Thinking as narrative feature jury winner and states audience voting/results follow a distinct schedule.
implementation_decision: Do not assign audience recognition on the jury announcement date.

title: TIFF 2026 reporting
finding: Trade reporting identifies La Bola Negra as People’s Choice winner and distinguishes runners-up and other prizes. An official TIFF result page was not obtained in this pass.
implementation_decision: Secondary evidence only; keep in research ledger, not verified-primary event seeds.

title: ScreenSkills animation model maker
finding: Stop-motion model makers construct physical characters and objects; CG modellers create digital assets that can be rigged. Size, materials, timing and budget constrain designs.
implementation_decision: Build separate physical fabrication and digital model/rig tasks. Shared asset IDs propagate revisions into dependent shots.

title: ScreenSkills production manager
finding: Production managers organize schedules/budgets, breakdowns and resources; duties vary with production scale and genre.
implementation_decision: A hire changes scheduling capacity and delegated tasks, not a universal quality bonus.

title: ScreenSkills VFX animator
finding: VFX animation integrates with live-action plates and camera positions. Motion capture transfers performance into character animation.
implementation_decision: Plate/version/capture dependencies differ from voice casting and ordinary live-action acting.

title: ScreenSkills line producer
finding: Line production includes crew, money and shoot completion, followed by handoff to post-production supervision.
implementation_decision: Keep hiring, resource control, wrap and finishing responsibilities explicit.

title: Copyright Office audiovisual music explanation
finding: Composition synchronization and recording master-use permissions are separate. Audiovisual synchronization does not use the mechanical compulsory-license route.
implementation_decision: Metadata selection is not permission to distribute audio. Simulated clearance gameplay and actual package media rights are separate.

title: CMRRA synchronization FAQ
finding: Synchronization permissions are individually negotiated with the publisher or copyright owner; CMRRA does not currently provide that service.
implementation_decision: Do not install universal artist pay rates or a guaranteed one-price clearance button.

title: Decca Hamnet soundtrack
finding: The label identifies Max Richter’s Hamnet score and lists a January 9, 2026 product release date.
implementation_decision: This is a soundtrack-product date, not automatically the film premiere or first availability of every recording.

title: Recording Academy Sinners album
finding: The Recording Academy identifies Ludwig Göransson and Sinners as a 2026 score-soundtrack winner.
implementation_decision: Can substantiate composer/work link; ceremony date and full category roster are not imported here.

title: Macmillan Elantris
finding: Publisher description identifies Raoden, Sarene and Hrathen, with Elantris/Kae in Arelon central to the story.
implementation_decision: Replace Hoid-only autofill with a structured multi-viewpoint correction; never infer sole lead from name count.

title: Sanderson standalone overview
finding: The author describes Elantris through three interweaving viewpoints: Raoden, Sarene and Hrathen.
implementation_decision: The source itself supports an ensemble approach; antagonist/ally labels are interpretive and remain editable.

title: Sanderson Warbreaker annotation
finding: The author contrasts Vivenna’s disruptive character change with Siri’s more gradual development.
implementation_decision: A single global pacing label cannot fully describe multiple arcs; keep character-level progression separate.

title: ARRI ALEXA 35 technical page
finding: The manufacturer specifies a Super 35 sensor with 4608×3164 photosites and seventeen stops; supported maximum rates depend on recording mode/media.
implementation_decision: Store mode-specific constraints. Do not combine maximum resolution and maximum frame rate into a nonexistent mode.

title: Sony FX3 launch
finding: Sony describes the FX3 as a compact full-frame camera supporting up to 4K120p and an XLR handle.
implementation_decision: Use for mobility/capture choices; no manufacturer evidence of automatic creative-quality points.

title: Blackmagic 6K Pro specifications
finding: 6K Pro specifies active EF mount, Super 35 sensor, thirteen stops and 6144×3456 up to fifty fps. Higher frame rates use different formats.
implementation_decision: Lens compatibility and mode restrictions are real; current advertised prices are not historical prices.

title: Netflix camera requirements relocation
finding: The previous camera-documentation URL redirects to a JavaScript application whose requirements were not readable in this retrieval.
implementation_decision: Do not certify every listed camera as Netflix-approved or apply branded production requirements to all acquisitions.

title: W3C minimum target-size explanation
finding: WCAG 2.2 minimum target guidance uses twenty-four by twenty-four CSS pixels with defined exceptions. User zoom alone does not satisfy target-size requirements.
implementation_decision: Audit controls at rendered scale; choose a larger comfortable touch design target without mislabeling it a mandatory standard.

title: W3C reflow explanation
finding: Reflow guidance discusses vertically scrolling content at 320 CSS pixels, with applicable exceptions for inherently two-dimensional content.
implementation_decision: Keep desktop-like hierarchy on phones but test reflow and contained tables; shrinking everything is not proof of accessibility.
